title: IncomingCall
summary: An incoming call is a call-style notification that the system shows as a heads-up or full-screen ringing screen, on the lock screen too. Monarch ships no ringing banner; while the app is in the foreground it may show MonarchBanner instead.
whenToUse: Whenever the app receives a call: post a NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall notification in the call channel, with a full-screen intent for the lock screen. While the app is open, a MonarchBanner with Decline and Answer can be shown in addition.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a custom ringing screen or rely on an in-app banner alone: it cannot ring on the lock screen or while the app is in the background. For a message that is not a call, use an ordinary notification.
api: NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall(person: Person, declineIntent: PendingIntent, answerIntent: PendingIntent): NotificationCompat.CallStyle
NotificationCompat.Builder(context: Context, channelId: String).setStyle(style).setCategory(NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_CALL).setFullScreenIntent(intent: PendingIntent, highPriority: Boolean)

options.name: person
options.description: The caller, with a name and optionally an icon.

options.name: declineIntent
options.description: What Decline does: end the call in the app's call service.

options.name: answerIntent
options.description: What Answer does: open the call screen and connect.

states.name: heads-up
states.description: While the phone is in use, the system shows the call at the top of the screen with Decline and Answer.

states.name: full screen
states.description: On the lock screen, the full-screen intent opens the app's ringing activity.

states.name: in-app banner
states.description: While the app is in the foreground, a MonarchBanner with Decline and Answer may also be shown.

appearance: The notification is drawn by the system in its own colors. The in-app banner is a MonarchBanner in the info tone with a primary Answer and a danger Decline button, in every Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web IncomingCall is a banner with Decline and Answer that the product places and rings itself. On Android the system owns the ringing: a call-style notification, as iOS uses CallKit. androidx.core.telecom (CallsManager, for Bluetooth and car audio routing) is not a Monarch dependency; the app adds it if it needs it. "Answer with audio only" for a video call has no counterpart in CallStyle; the app can add an action.
accessibility: System behavior: the call notification and the ringing screen are accessible, announce the caller and work with TalkBack.
The in-app banner is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces the call; its buttons have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: From Android 13 posting needs the POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission, and from Android 14 a full-screen intent needs USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT; check both before posting.
Create the call notification channel with high importance before posting; on Android 8 and later the channel sets the sound and the heads-up.
A call-style notification must be shown from a foreground service of type phoneCall, or use a full-screen intent, or the system shows it as an ordinary notification.
The example and the catalogue page were compiled and composed; the notification was not posted on a device.

examples.title: Audio call
Post the incoming call notification
examples.code:
MonarchButton(
    text = "Simulate an incoming call",
    onClick = {
        val manager = NotificationManagerCompat.from(context)
        manager.createNotificationChannel(
            NotificationChannelCompat.Builder("calls", NotificationManagerCompat.IMPORTANCE_HIGH)
                .setName("Calls")
                .build(),
        )
        // The app's call activity; here the app's launch screen stands in for it.
        val open = PendingIntent.getActivity(
            context,
            0,
            Intent(Intent.ACTION_MAIN).setPackage(context.packageName),
            PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE,
        )
        val caller = Person.Builder().setName("Ana Flores").setImportant(true).build()
        val notification = NotificationCompat.Builder(context, "calls")
            // Here the app icon; a real app passes its monochrome notification icon, R.drawable.….
            .setSmallIcon(context.applicationInfo.icon)
            .setStyle(NotificationCompat.CallStyle.forIncomingCall(caller, open, open))
            .setCategory(NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_CALL)
            .setFullScreenIntent(open, true)
            .build()
        val allowed = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU ||
            ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS) ==
            PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        if (allowed) manager.notify(1, notification)
    },
    variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Primary,
)
